text:
A match that should have been about 103 was instead about four. Andy Robertson is due huge acclaim for becoming the most capped player in Scotland’s history but how the full-back will wish the moment arrived in different circumstances. A second string Switzerland team pulled Scotland apart, raising further and significant questions about the suitability of Sébastien Pocognoli to carry out the job his paymasters boldly entrusted him with. Scottish FA giddiness about Pocognoli as the successor to Steve Clarke, a hugely successful leader of the national team, is looking increasingly ridiculous.
This was a horrible night for Pocognoli, who is under serious pressure just three months into his tenure. Scotland’s players looked a rudderless, disillusioned lot. Pocognoli has never previously managed in international football, which renders it reasonable to ask his qualifications to improve this grim scenario. Scotland have finished a distant third in a favourable Nations League section. Ramifications exist for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw in December. Pocognoli is taking a pounding in the court of public opinion.
Pocognoli’s demeanour and tone during pre-match media duties suggested he may be well aware of and irritated by the early questioning of his tactical approach. The Belgian is unwilling to deviate from the deployment of three centre-backs whether Scotland are at home to North Macedonia or away to Switzerland. A harsh reality, whether Pocognoli chose to accept it or not, is Scotland had generally failed to convince during his five previous games in charge. While the prospect of facing a highly impressive Swiss team would ordinarily make Scots gulp, there was cause for hope in St Gallen. Not only had Switzerland already won Group B1 but they were in makeshift form here. A much-needed break for Pocognoli?
Switzerland’s lack of cohesion was apparent during an opening spell where the visitors looked comfortable. A flurry of set pieces and a John McGinn half volley that dipped over Yvon Mvogo’s crossbar emphasised Scottish attacking intent. On a difficult pitch, Switzerland’s first 20 minutes lacked purpose. It soon looked that may be as good as things got for Scotland.
There appeared no real danger as Zachary Athekame fired in a hopeful cross from the Swiss right. Scotland had an abundance of cover inside their own penalty area. The problem was that one of those charged with clearing lines, Lewis Ferguson, instead poked the ball past Angus Gunn. No own goals are pretty; this one was especially ugly. Ferguson had needlessly panicked. Scotland assisted the Swiss with an early red card when these teams met in Glasgow. The acts of kindness had continued.
Scotland attempted an immediate response as Aaron Hickey headed wide. The Brentford man had to be withdrawn before the interval, apparently damaging his left hamstring when making a defensive intervention. Hickey, whose career has been seriously disrupted by injury, was understandably distraught. Albeit Switzerland were by now in control, McGinn spurned glorious opportunity five minutes before the interval when heading straight at Mvogo. Adrian Bajrami spared McGinn’s blushes with an even worse miss at the opposite end before the teams headed for their orange wedges. The half had been humdrum in nature.
Ferguson’s bizarre shanking of the ball out for a Switzerland corner set the tone for a spell where the game was put firmly out of Scotland’s reach. Samuel Ballet burst forward from midfield before playing a one-two with Remo Freuler and slamming towards the Scotland net. The ball was heading in before Winsley Boteli made certain, with the VAR dismissing Scotland appeals for offside. The ease with which Ballet evaded those in navy blue was as striking as the space Freuler found himself in. Scotland’s organisation, once a staple, was nonexistent. Five defenders and two deep lying midfielders were being gleefully ignored by the rampaging Swiss.
Number three was another Scotland horror show. Nathan Patterson, Hickey’s replacement, was dispossessed by Boteli. The forward found Alvyn Sanches, who angled a shot across Gunn. So, so easy. Gunn’s positioning was questionable.
Scott McTominay, again peripheral, slammed over when it looked easier to score a Scotland consolation. Scottish fans jeered at the point of one sideways pass too many in defence. Many headed for the exit as Zeki Amdouni’s shot deflected off Luke Graham and beyond Gunn.
A year ago, Scotland were celebrating World Cup qualification on the most epic of Hampden Park nights as Denmark were vanquished. It is so difficult to square that occasion with 90 minutes in St Gallen. Scotland look a team in ghastly regression.
digest_he:
נבחרת שווייץ רשמה ניצחון קליל של 4:0 מול סקוטלנד במסגרת משחקי ליגת האומות, תוצאה שהעמידה את מאמן סקוטלנד, סבסטיאן פוקוניולי, תחת לחץ כבד זמן קצר לאחר מינויו. המשחק כלל שער עצמי של לואיס פרגוסון במחצית הראשונה, פציעה של ארון היקי, ושערים נוספים במחצית השנייה מצידם של וינסלי בוטלי, אלבין סאנצ'ס וזקי אמדוני.

ההפסד חותם קמפיין מאכזב עבור הסקוטים, שסיימו במקום השלישי בבית ובכך נפגעו סיכוייהם לקראת הגרלת מוקדמות יורו 2028. עבור פוקוניולי, שהחליף בתפקיד את סטיב קלארק, מדובר בפתיחת קדנציה רצופת קשיים עם שני ניצחונות בלבד בשישה משחקים מול יריבות נחותות, מה שמעורר סימני שאלה רבים בקרב הקהל והתקשורת בנוגע לעתידו בנבחרת.
